citations.title: Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities
citations.requirement: Lists 18 personal rights: dignity; freedom from punishment, humiliation, intimidation or abuse; being told how to complain to CCLD and the ombudsman; leaving at any time and not being locked in; private visits by ombudsmen and advocates at reasonable hours without prior notice; keeping and spending own money; phone, mail, voting and refusing care; moving out. Subsection (b) bars denial of admission, transfer, discharge, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, preferred name or pronouns, and association, based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Subsection (d): the Department cannot waive the (b) protections.

citations.title: Emergency Disaster Plan
citations.requirement: A written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan. It must cover: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies; and notifying a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation. Emergency exit plans and telephone numbers must be posted.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements-General
citations.requirement: Personnel must be sufficient in numbers and competent. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need. Anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older. Staff assisting with personal ADLs get initial and annual training under HSC §§1569.625 and 1569.69, plus first aid from a qualified provider. Required training topics are listed, with trainer qualifications and documentation in personnel records. All personnel need a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test) within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is required before employment or presence. Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan.

citations.title: Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services
citations.requirement: Requires a plan for incidental medical and dental care. Staff may only assist with self-administered medications and may not give injections unless authorized by law. Assistance cannot include forcing, hiding or camouflaging medications. PRN rules: a signed, dated physician order on a prescription blank, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours. Central storage in a locked place, in the original container, with a record kept at least 1 year. Destruction by the administrator and one other non-resident adult, with a record kept at least 3 years. First aid kit; emergency numbers posted; ambulance number available; call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health.

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Individual written agreement in 12-point type, plain language, with titled sections. Signed and dated within 7 days of admission. Copy given immediately, and a copy or notice of availability posted. Must specify basic services, additional services, rates, payment, 60 days' written notice of rate changes, refund conditions, preadmission fee limits and refunds, visiting policy, firearms policy, grievance procedure, eviction grounds and notice rights, and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman. LIC 9158 is required when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability. No liability-waiver provisions.

citations.title: Prohibited Health Conditions
citations.requirement: Residents who need health services for, or have, these conditions cannot be admitted or retained: stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy tubes, naso-gastric tubes, staph or other serious infection, total dependence on others for all ADLs, and tracheostomies. The list is not exhaustive ("including, but not limited to").

citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: (a)(1) Written report to the licensing agency and the person responsible for the resident within 7 days of any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, or any incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse). (a)(2) Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: within 24 hours by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer. (a)(3) Fires and explosions: immediately to the local fire authority, and no later than the next working day to the licensing agency. (b),(c) Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult: report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours. (d),(e),(f) Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice; notice to applicants before signing; civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000. (g) Notice of a new administrator within 30 days. (h) Change of chief corporate officer within 15 working days.

citations.title: Night Supervision (RCFE)
citations.requirement: Fewer than 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises overnight. 16–100 residents: one employee awake on duty plus one on call within 10 minutes. Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained. (Per fact-checked research S7.)

citations.title: Care of Persons with Dementia
citations.requirement: In homes with fewer than 16 beds, at least one night staff person must be awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation. (Per fact-checked research S8.)

citations.title: Advertising Dementia Special Care
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises dementia care must have a written dementia program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators. Keep advertisements for 3 years. (Per fact-checked research S27 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Written plan covering purposes and goals, admission agreement, admission policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, handling of resident money, visiting policy, approach to resident behavioral expression, and the infection control plan. (Per fact-checked research S23.)

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Fire clearance is required before licensure. A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents. (Per fact-checked research S28.)

citations.title: Personal Accommodations and Services
citations.requirement: No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family. (Per fact-checked research S24.)

citations.title: Maintenance and Operation
citations.requirement: Heat of at least 68°F; hot water 105–120°F; plant maintenance standards; private water supply testing (annually for capacity 7–15). (Per fact-checked research S69 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption is required for the applicant, administrator, adult household members and staff before they work or are present. (Per fact-checked research S29.)

citations.title: Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables
citations.requirement: If the facility holds resident cash, it must keep receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as the residents' money, with no commingling. LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond. (Per fact-checked research S70.)

citations.title: Administrator-Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Administrator must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent and good character, and must be certified. Added education and experience for 16+ beds. Must be on premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent. (Per fact-checked research S14.)

citations.title: Infection Control Requirements
citations.requirement: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282). Name an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional. Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration, or at the licensing agency's request. (Per fact-checked research S32.)

citations.title: Hospice Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request. (Per fact-checked research S26.)

citations.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal
citations.requirement: Pre-admission interview and functional, mental and social evaluation, with consent and a suitability determination against admission criteria before admission. (Per fact-checked research S35 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Administrator certification
citations.requirement: 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and state exam within 60 days. 40 hours of CE every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia. (Per fact-checked research S13.)

citations.title: Direct care staff training
citations.requirement: 40 hours initial: 20 before working alone and 20 within 4 weeks. The first 20 include 6 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. 20 hours annually, including 8 hours dementia. (Per fact-checked research S10.)

citations.title: Dementia training for direct care staff
citations.requirement: Dementia training for direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S11.)

citations.title: Medication assistance training
citations.requirement: Homes of 15 or fewer: 10 hours initial (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. Homes of 16+: 24 hours initial (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S12.)

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: Care custodians and facility staff are mandated reporters. Report by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible, then in writing within the statutory time (SOC 341). The facility-specific 2-hour and 24-hour timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c). (Per fact-checked research S36.)

citations.title: Liability insurance minimums
citations.requirement: Liability insurance of $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence. (Per fact-checked research S18.)

citations.title: HCBS Settings Rule (applies to Assisted Living Waiver settings)
citations.requirement: HCBS settings must include a lease or agreement, privacy, resident choice, and access to food and visitors. Applies only if the RCFE enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver. (Per fact-checked research.)

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Annual fee of $495.60 (4–6 beds) or $742.80 (7–15 beds), due each license anniversary, with a 50% late fee. Capacity change fee of $25. (Per fact-checked research S1.)

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: At least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year. (Per fact-checked research S57.)

citations.title: Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly
citations.requirement: Special meal and rest period rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel. (Per fact-checked research S60.)

citations.cite: LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B
citations.title: Application attachments (theft and loss policy B14; neighborhood complaint policy B15; sample menu B10; job descriptions B4–B5)
citations.requirement: Written theft and loss policy (B14); neighborhood complaint policy when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer (B15); sample menu (B10); job descriptions and personnel policies (B4–B5). (Per fact-checked research S21.)

citations.title: Workers' compensation coverage
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation insurance is required once the facility has employees; RCFEs are WCIRB class 9070(1). Cited in the fact-checked checklist; the section text was not fetched here and the URL is a code-index link only.

policies.title: Emergency Disaster Plan, Relocation Sites and Posted Exit Plans
state_specifics: Use LIC 610E (RCFE version). The plan must name two relocation sites away from the facility, each able to hold every resident.
If the applicant does not currently occupy a relocation site, get written authorization from the person or agency in possession and keep it verified in writing.
Cover staff assignments, fire safety plan, exits, assembly site, transportation, supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation.
Notify a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation.
Post emergency exit plans and emergency telephone numbers.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Fire clearance is required before licensure.
A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents.
Report fires and explosions immediately to the local fire authority, and to licensing no later than the next working day.
Drill frequency and documentation come from 22 CCR §87203. Its text was not retrieved, so confirm it before publishing.

policies.title: Job Descriptions by Staff Classification
state_specifics: Write one job description per classification. Each must match a classification on the LIC 500 Personnel Report.
State duties and responsibilities in clear, concise terms.

State minimum qualifications that track licensing rules. Administrator: 21 or older, HS diploma or equivalent, certified. Anyone supervising staff or residents: 18 or older. Include first aid, medication assistance and dementia training requirements.
State lines of supervision, given and received, for every position.
Include an awake night shift duty statement.

policies.title: Personnel Policies, Work Hours, Shift Coverage and Night Supervision
state_specifics: No numeric day ratio. Staff must be sufficient in numbers and competent, and CDSS may require more when documentation shows a need.
Fewer than 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises overnight.
Awake night staff are required when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation.
Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained.
Shifts and work days must match the LIC 500 Personnel Report. Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers are supervised and not counted.

policies.title: Employee Abuse-Reporting Responsibilities
state_specifics: Tell every employee in writing of their duty to report to the licensing agency, law enforcement and the adult protective agency or ombudsman.
Suspected physical abuse with serious bodily injury: report within 2 hours. Otherwise within 24 hours.
Written report on SOC 341. Report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and law enforcement.
Employees sign an acknowledgment at hire and annually.

policies.title: Hiring, Screening and Conditions of Employment
state_specifics: Screen applicants for required education and experience.

Tell employees that employment is conditioned on DOJ/FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption, a criminal conviction statement (LIC 508), TB clearance, a physician health screening or health questionnaire, and any index checks required by licensing.
No one may be employed or present before criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer.
Applicant, administrator and adult household members also need clearance.

policies.title: Employee Health Screening, TB Testing and Personnel Records
state_specifics: Physician health screening with chest x-ray or intradermal TB test, no more than 6 months before or 7 days after employment (LIC 503).
Personnel records (LIC 501) hold training documentation, health screening and criminal record clearance.
Training documentation, trainer qualifications and sign-in sheets go in the personnel file.
Keep files current for quarterly mock inspections. §87412 text was not retrieved, so confirm retention before publishing.

policies.title: Wage and Hour, Paid Sick Leave, Meal and Rest Periods
state_specifics: California minimum wage is $16.90/hr from 1/1/2026. Pay the higher local minimum where one applies (e.g., City of Los Angeles $18.42 and San Francisco $19.61 from 7/1/2026).
Paid sick leave: at least 40 hours or 5 days per year.
Wage Order 5 has special meal and rest rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care of the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shift arrangements need employment counsel.
The SB 525 health-care minimum wage applies only if the RCFE is affiliated with or controlled by an acute-care hospital.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff are trained on resident personal rights.
Prohibit punishment, humiliation, intimidation and abuse.
Prohibit staff from accepting resident funds or valuables except under the resident cash and theft-and-loss policies.
Prohibit discrimination based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status.

policies.title: New Employee Orientation and Initial Training
state_specifics: Submit the in-service training plan with the plan of operation, naming who conducts the training and their qualifications.
Direct care staff: 40 hours initial. 20 hours before working alone (including 6 dementia and 4 postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice), 20 more within 4 weeks (including 6 dementia).
Medication assistance, homes of 15 or fewer: 10 hours (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam.
First aid from a qualified provider. Night staff are first-aid trained.

policies.title: Ongoing In-Service Training, Administrator Continuing Education and Documentation
state_specifics: Direct care staff: 20 hours annually, including 8 dementia and 4 postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. Staff assisting with medications: 8 hours annually.
Administrator: 40 hours CE every 2 years, including 8 on dementia. List administrator CE in the plan.
The plan must include the topics in 22 CCR §80065 and §87565, as LIC 281 requires. The text of those sections was not retrieved, so confirm the topic list.
State how often training is given and how it is documented (sign-in sheets, trainer qualifications, personnel file).

policies.title: Program Description, Philosophy and Hours of Operation
state_specifics: Give a general overview of philosophy, services and activities. A brochure is acceptable only if it includes every element B7.1 to B7.11.
State the purpose, goals and program methods.
Operation is 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The same text may also appear in the admission policies.
Keep the program description consistent with the plan of operation.

policies.title: Basic and Optional Services
state_specifics: Describe basic services using the list in Admission Guideline LIC 604/604A.
List optional services exactly as they appear in the admission agreement, with rates.
Rate changes need 60 days' written notice.
Basic services in §87464 are title-confirmed only, so check the text before publishing.

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Write a daily schedule of activities, stating who plans, conducts and assists residents.
Attach a one-month calendar of social, educational and recreational activities, also naming who plans, conducts and assists.
Adapt activities for residents with dementia.
The text of §87219 (Planned Activities) was not retrieved, so confirm its requirements.

policies.title: Medical Emergencies, Change of Condition and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health, subject to the advance directive exceptions in §87469.
Keep the first aid kit stocked. Post emergency numbers and keep the ambulance number available.
Notify the physician and the person responsible for the resident of a change of condition.
Serious injury, AED use or a death needs a written report within 7 days to licensing and the person responsible.
Outbreaks, poisonings and major accidents: report within 24 hours.

policies.title: Assistance with Self-Administered Medications
state_specifics: Staff may only assist with self-administered medications. No injections unless authorized by law.
Never force, hide or camouflage medications.
PRN orders must be signed and dated on a prescription blank, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours.
Only staff who completed the medication training and exam may assist.

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Plan of operation must describe transportation arrangements.
State who provides transport (facility vehicle, contractor, family), for medical appointments and outings.
Verify driver license and auto insurance for anyone transporting residents.
Include transport in the emergency disaster plan.

policies.title: Community Resources, Consultants, Hospice and Home Health
state_specifics: List community resources and consultants: physicians, pharmacy, home health, hospice, local ombudsman, county adult protective services.
Hospice care in the facility requires a hospice care waiver. Submit a written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents. CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request.
Coordinate care plans with hospice or home health in writing.
If the RCFE enrolls in the Assisted Living Waiver, list the care coordination agencies and the licensed nurse resource.

policies.title: Immediate Response to Incidents and Complaints (Licensing-Approved Procedure)
state_specifics: Submit a written procedure for immediate response to incidents and complaints.
Name who takes the report, who investigates and the time frames for follow-up.
Link to the reporting deadlines in 22 CCR §87211.
Keep a log of each incident or complaint and its resolution.

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: Homes under 16 beds: at least one night staff person awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake supervision.
Advertising dementia care requires a written dementia program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators.
Keep ads for 3 years.
Dementia training: 6 hours in each of the first two 20-hour blocks, 8 hours annually.

policies.category: B8 Rules of Discipline / Personal Rights
policies.title: Personal Rights of Residents
state_specifics: Inform residents and representatives of their personal rights at admission and post the rights.
State plainly that rights will not be violated.

Rights include dignity, freedom from abuse, being told how to complain to licensing and the ombudsman, leaving at any time and not being locked in, private visits, keeping and spending own money, phone, mail, voting and refusing care.
Train staff on residents' rights (§87468; text not retrieved).

policies.category: B8 Rules of Discipline / Personal Rights
policies.title: Rules of Conduct, No Corporal or Unusual Punishment, and Restraints
state_specifics: Include a clear statement that no corporal or unusual punishment will be used.
No punishment, humiliation or intimidation of residents.
Policies must not violate personal rights.
The group-home discipline items in LIC 281 B8 do not apply to RCFEs.
Postural supports and restraints follow §87608 (title confirmed only). Confirm text and get physician and CDSS approvals as required.

policies.category: B8 Rules of Discipline / Personal Rights
policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Do not deny admission or transfer, discharge, assign rooms or restrooms, or restrict preferred name or pronouns or association based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status.
CDSS cannot waive these protections.
Use LIC 9158 when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability.
Provide interpretation or translation for residents with limited English.

policies.title: Persons Accepted, Compatibility and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: State the age range served (RCFE Act age rule: confirm HSC §1569.2 text before publishing) and how compatibility with current residents is decided.
Admission policies include rates and refund policies, acceptance and retention limits, appraisals, needs and services plans, medical assessments and the admission agreement.
Do not admit anyone with a prohibited health condition under §87615.
Decide admission by documented suitability under §87456 (title confirmed only).

policies.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal and Placement Appropriateness
state_specifics: Pre-admission interview with a functional, mental and social evaluation, with the resident's consent.
Document the suitability decision against admission criteria before admission.
B9.2 (intake for group homes) does not apply. This RCFE intake procedure replaces it.
Describe interviews and how paperwork is obtained and developed.

policies.title: Medical Assessment, Physical Examination, TB and Immunization Requirements
state_specifics: Require a medical assessment by a physician and a physical exam with TB testing before or at admission, per §87458 (title confirmed only; confirm text).
State any resident immunization requirement the facility applies.
Keep medical documents in the resident record.
Staff TB and health screening is covered separately in PP-04.

policies.title: Needs and Services Plan and Reappraisal
state_specifics: Prepare a needs and services plan from the appraisal.
Reappraise on change of condition and at the intervals in §87463 (title confirmed only; confirm text).
Involve the resident and representative in decisions (§87467).
Use the reappraisal to adjust night supervision for dementia.

policies.title: Emergency Information and Sign-In/Sign-Out
state_specifics: Collect emergency contacts, physician, hospice and medical information at admission.
Residents may leave at any time and may not be locked in.
Log residents leaving and returning, with time and expected return.
Link the sign-out procedure to the missing resident procedure (SAF-03).

policies.title: Retention Limits and Prohibited Health Conditions
state_specifics: Cannot admit or retain residents with stage 3 or 4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy or naso-gastric tubes, tracheostomies, staph or other serious infection, or total dependence on others for all ADLs. The list is not exhaustive.
Hospice residents are retained only under the hospice waiver rules (§87632).
Allowable conditions and exceptions: §§87609 to 87617 (titles only; confirm text).
Relocation orders and review: §§87637 to 87639 (titles only).

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Rates, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: 12-point type, plain language, titled sections. Signed and dated within 7 days of admission, with a copy given immediately.
Specify basic and additional services, rates, payment, refunds and preadmission fee limits.
60 days' written notice of rate changes.
Include the visiting and firearms policies, grievance procedure, eviction grounds and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman.
No liability-waiver provisions.

policies.title: Discharge, Eviction and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Eviction grounds and wording come from §87224 and may not be modified, except general house policies under §87224(a)(3).
Department-ordered relocation is under §87223.
The admission agreement must state eviction grounds and notice rights.
Residents may move out at any time.
Full text of §87223 and §87224 was not retrieved. Confirm notice periods before publishing.

policies.title: Sample Menu, Meal Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Plan meals and snacks for one week using the four basic food groups.
State portion sizes and the times meals are served.
Serve therapeutic diets only on physician order.
Food Services rules are in Chapter 8, Article 10. Section numbers were not retrieved, so pull the text before finalizing storage and diet content.

policies.title: Control of Property, Lease and Ownership Documentation
state_specifics: State the name and address of the property owner.
Lease or rental agreement must not preclude facility use or compliance with regulations.
If the applicant owns the property, provide a deed or property tax bill showing the facility street address.
Local zoning treats homes serving 6 or fewer as residential. Homes of 7 or more should confirm with the planning department.

policies.title: Physical Plant, Maintenance, Housekeeping and Laundry
state_specifics: No more than 2 residents per bedroom. At least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family.
Heat at least 68°F. Hot water 105 to 120°F.
Test a private water supply annually for capacity 7 to 15.
Nonambulatory or bedridden residents need the fire clearance first.

policies.title: Insurance Information and Coverage
state_specifics: State whether insurance covers the facility operation, and the coverage type and carrier. If none, a statement saying so is sufficient for the application.
Liability insurance minimums: $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence.
Workers' compensation is required once there are employees. §3700 text was not fetched, so confirm before publishing.

policies.category: B14 Theft and Loss Policy (RCFE only)
policies.title: Theft and Loss Policy
state_specifics: Inventory personal property at admission and modify the inventory as items change.
Safeguard personal property on the resident's death.
Document and report any loss of personal property.
State the method for marking personal property and for providing a secure area for safekeeping.
The text of §87218 was not retrieved, so confirm it.

policies.category: B14 Theft and Loss Policy (RCFE only)
policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property Safeguards
state_specifics: If the facility holds resident cash, file the LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond.
Keep receipts and accounting records, and a separate account titled as residents' money. No commingling.
Residents may keep and spend their own money.
Commingling and bonding sections: §§87213, 87215 and 87216 (titles only; confirm text).

policies.category: B15 Neighborhood Complaint Policy (six or fewer, non-resident owner)
policies.title: Neighborhood Complaint Policy
state_specifics: Required when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer. Confirm applicability for your facility.
State procedures for immediate response to incidents and complaints.
State a set time when the owner, licensee or designee will meet with neighbors.
Keep a complaint log.

policies.title: Governing Body, Licensee and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: A certified administrator (21 or older, HS diploma, good character) is on the premises enough hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent (LIC 308).
Certification: 80-hour program, state exam, 40 hours CE every 2 years.
Notify licensing within 30 days of a new administrator, and within 15 working days of a change of chief corporate officer.
Governing body accountability: §87205 (title only; confirm text).

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Advertising
state_specifics: Post the license, resident rights, ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 with the local ombudsman number, and exit plans.
Annual fee $495.60 (4 to 6 beds) or $742.80 (7 to 15), due each license anniversary. 50% late fee.
Capacity change fee $25.
Show the license number in advertisements (§87206; confirm text).

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Quality Assurance
state_specifics: Review the plan of operation and policies at least annually and when rules change.
Run quarterly mock inspections of medication records, personnel files, appraisals and admission agreements.
Review the infection control plan annually, after an outbreak declaration or at licensing request.
Program flexibility requests: §87209 (title only).

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Billing Integrity and Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver
state_specifics: Prohibit false claims or misrepresentation to residents and regulators.
If enrolled in the ALW, settings must meet the HCBS rule: lease or agreement, privacy, choice, access to food and visitors.
ALW does not pay room and board. The resident pays it, typically the SSI/SSP basic services rate ($1,444.07/mo in 2026).
ALW providers need licensed nursing staff on call or employed.

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Post the Long-Term Care Ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local ombudsman number.
Residents have private visits by ombudsmen and advocates at reasonable hours without prior notice.
Tell residents how to complain to CDSS Community Care Licensing (ASCP (916) 657-2592).
The grievance procedure appears in the admission agreement.
No retaliation.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Safeguard resident records and limit disclosure to those authorized.
HIPAA applies if the facility is a covered entity, for example when billing Medi-Cal electronically.
Residents have a right to private phone, mail and visits.
Obtain written release before sharing records outside required reporting.

policies.title: Medication Storage, PRN, Records and Disposal
state_specifics: Keep medications in locked central storage in the original container.
Keep the medication record at least 1 year.
Destruction by the administrator and one other non-resident adult. Keep the destruction record at least 3 years.
Medication-assist training: 10 hours for homes of 15 or fewer, 24 hours for 16+, plus an exam.

policies.title: Nursing Services, Delegation and ALW Licensed Nurse Oversight
state_specifics: Staff provide only incidental medical care within §87465. No injections unless authorized by law.
Healing wounds and other restricted conditions follow §§87631 and 87609 to 87613 (titles only; confirm text).
ALW providers need licensed nurse oversight on call or employed.
Facilities housing more than 6 ALW participants need an Individual Response System.

policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries are prohibited conditions. Transfer if one develops.
Observe residents for changes (§87466; title only).
Care of bedridden residents is §87606 (title only). It requires the separate fire clearance.
Use postural supports only per §87608 and a physician order; confirm text.

policies.title: Advance Directives, Resuscitative Requests and Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Honor advance directives and resuscitative-measure requests under §87469 (title confirmed; confirm text).
A death must be reported in writing within 7 days to licensing and the person responsible.
Notify the hospice agency and physician.
Safeguard personal property on a resident's death.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Staff are mandated reporters under W&I Code §15630.
Report by phone to law enforcement within 2 hours for serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours, then SOC 341 in writing.
Send reports to the ombudsman, licensing agency and law enforcement.
Residents have the right to be free from abuse and intimidation.

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Written report to licensing and the person responsible within 7 days of any death, serious injury, AED use or incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse).
Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: phone or fax to licensing and the local health officer within 24 hours.
Fires and explosions: immediately to the fire authority, and licensing by the next working day.
Keep an internal incident log.

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Residents may not be locked in, so use supervision and the appraisal, not locks.
Search immediately, then call law enforcement and notify the person responsible if the resident is not found.
Unexplained absence is a reportable incident (7-day written report).
Awake night supervision for dementia residents who wander.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282) with a trained Infection Control Lead.
Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration or at licensing request.
Outbreaks: report within 24 hours to licensing and the local health officer.
Staff health and TB screening per PP-04.

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: The visiting policy and firearms policy must appear in the admission agreement.
Residents have private visits and ombudsman access without prior notice.
State where smoking is permitted, if at all.
Pets: set vaccination and supervision rules.

policies.title: Resident Records, Register and Retention
state_specifics: Keep resident records and the register of residents (§§87506 and 87508; text not retrieved, so do not state general retention periods until read).
Medication records at least 1 year. Destruction records at least 3 years.
Keep dementia advertisements 3 years.
Keep the signed admission agreement and appraisal in the record.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Death, serious injury, AED use or other incident: 7 days in writing.
Outbreaks, poisonings and major accidents: within 24 hours. Suspected abuse: 2 hours or 24 hours.
Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice. Civil penalty $100 per day, up to $2,000.
New administrator: 30 days. Change of chief corporate officer: 15 working days.
Annual license fee on time. Notify CDSS before a capacity change.

documents.title: Application Instructions for A Facility License (Section B supportive documents; Section A14 emergency disaster plan). Covers Adult Residential, Group Homes, Small Family Homes, RCFE, RCF-CI, and others.
documents.issuer: California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Community Care Licensing Division
documents.version: Item text below is from LIC 281 (9/04), the owner-supplied copy, which I re-read in full on the CDSS site. The CDSS Forms I-L page now lists a newer LIC 281 (11/25), but its PDF returned 'no permission' on every fetch. I could not compare it with the 9/04 text, so confirm that no items changed.
documents.url: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/cdssweb/entres/forms/english/lic281.pdf (9/04 text read). Current 11/25 edition, not retrievable: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Portals/9/Additional-Resources/Forms-and-Brochures/2020/I-L/LIC281.pdf?ver=cDy_GGClLQ7_6gtjxO-jNQ%3d%3d (listed at https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/forms-brochures/forms-alphabetic-list/i-l)
documents.how_used: This is the checklist-style document CDSS uses to review an RCFE applicant's written Section B items. Items are taken from the Section B table (RCFE column) and the B4-B15 narrative instructions. A14 is added from Section A because it is a required written plan. The source bullets are unnumbered, so I added sequence suffixes (e.g., B4.1) in the order they appear.

required_items.text: Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610D; for RCFE only, LIC 610E). The plan must show two relocation sites away from the facility that can accommodate the number of clients in the facility.
required_items.cite: LIC 281 (9/04) p.2 (Section A table) and p.9, A14

required_items.text: If the property is not currently occupied by the applicant, use of the relocation site requires authorization from the agency or person currently in possession, verified in writing.

JOB DESCRIPTIONS: a job description for each staff classification. Each must be clear, concise and relevant to the position, and must match a classification on the Personnel Report (LIC 500). Staff positions must correspond to those listed on all personnel reports.
Duties and responsibilities.
Minimum qualifications that correspond to licensing requirements, including any special licenses, certificates or special skills needed to perform the job.
Lines of supervision, including supervision given and to whom, and supervision received and from whom.
PERSONNEL POLICIES: describe the regulatory requirements commonly associated with personnel practices, such as staff coverage, staff qualifications, work schedules and conditions of employment.
Work hours/shifts, to document that positions provide coverage with competent staff. They must correspond with the staff positions and work days and hours listed on all personnel reports.
Abuse reporting procedures. Documentation must indicate that employees will be informed of their responsibility to report to the licensing agency, the police, and the child/adult protective agency.

Hiring practices, including screening of employees for necessary education and experience. Employees must be informed that conditions of employment include fingerprint clearance, statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance, physical examination/health questionnaire, and child abuse index check.
IN-SERVICE TRAINING FOR STAFF: a plan for in-service training, submitted to the licensing agency at the time of application as part of the plan of operation.
New employee training: a description of the training, stating who will conduct it.

Ongoing training: topics to be covered (the list should include administrator continuing education units), how often the training will be given, and how it will be documented. It must include the topics specified in regulation sections 80065 (General) and 87565 (Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly).

RCFE PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: a general overview of the program philosophies, services provided and activities in the facility. A pamphlet or brochure is acceptable only if it includes all of the following elements (B7.1-B7.11).
Brief statement of the purpose, goals and program methods (program philosophy).
Days and hours of operation (**may also appear in the Admission Policies section).
Daily schedule of activities to be provided by the facility, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
A one-month schedule of planned social, educational and recreational activities, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
Description of the basic services provided by the facility (** may also appear in the Admission Policies section; see Admission Guideline LIC 604/604A for the list of basic services).
Description of the optional services provided in the facility, as listed in the admission agreement (** may also appear in the Admission Policies section).
Description of how the facility will handle medical emergencies if a client becomes ill or injured.
Procedure for handling and assisting clients/residents with self-administered medications.
Transportation arrangements.
Description of community resources and consultants to be used by the facility.
A procedure, approved by the licensing agency, for immediate response to incidents and complaints.

RULES OF DISCIPLINE / PERSONAL RIGHTS. Personal rights apply to all facility categories. The detailed discipline items (types of discipline used and conditions, types not permitted, 'no corporal punishment/violation of personal rights', conferences with parents/placement representatives, grounds for dismissal/eviction/relocation/removal) are headed 'Group Homes and Foster Family Agencies only'. CDSS will evaluate the policies to ensure they do not violate personal rights and contain a clear statement that no corporal or unusual punishment will be used.

ADMISSION POLICIES: must provide information relevant to the category of clients accepted for care, including ages of clients, rates and refund policies, acceptance and retention limitations, pre-admission appraisals, needs and services plans, medical assessments, and an admission agreement containing the typical information a client or authorized representative needs before entering. A description of the following items (B9.1-B9.11) must be included.
Persons accepted for care, including age range and compatibility determination process, when necessary.
Intake procedures for placement in group homes (listed in the shared list; written for the group home category).
Criteria for assessing appropriateness of placement given an individual client's needs (i.e., interviews, procedures for obtaining and developing the necessary paperwork, etc.).
Needs and services plan.
Client's Rights/Personal Rights. At a minimum, a statement that clients/residents will be informed of their rights and that their rights will not be violated.
Medical assessment.
Pre-admission appraisal plan.
Emergency information.
Sign-in and sign-out procedures.
Immunization requirements.
Physical examination requirements (including TB testing).
SAMPLE MENU, to show the applicant is familiar with balanced meals, acceptable portion sizes and general principles of good nutrition. It will include the items B10.1-B10.3.
Planned meals and snacks for one week, using foods from the four basic food groups.
Portion sizes.
Times meals served.
CONTROL OF PROPERTY: name and address of the owner of the facility property.
Copy of the lease or rental agreement (no requirement on its length). The agreement must not preclude use of the property as a facility or prevent compliance with regulations.
Proof of ownership if the applicant owns the property (property tax bill, deed or similar). The document must show the facility street address.
INSURANCE INFORMATION (RCFE only): a statement on whether insurance will cover the facility operation. If so, state the type of coverage and with whom. If not, a statement saying so is sufficient.

THEFT AND LOSS POLICY (RCFE only). The policy shall include provisions for: inventory of personal property at admission; modification of the inventory; practices to safeguard personal property upon the resident's death; documentation and reporting of loss of personal property; method of marking personal property; and method for providing a secure area for safekeeping of resident personal property.

NEIGHBORHOOD COMPLAINT POLICY: procedures for immediate response to incidents and complaints, including a time when the owner, licensee or designee will be available to meet with neighborhood residents. Applies only to non-resident-owner community care facilities providing residential care for six or fewer persons. The Section B table marks it 'Required' in the Adult Residential/RCFE column, so confirm applicability for your facility.

official.notes: LIC 281 says to submit the Section A and B documents in the same sequence as the booklet. Organize the manual by the B-numbers above, with the A14 plan in its Section A position. The booklet says the application fee plus the Section A and B documents go to the licensing agency as one packet. Incomplete packets are returned in full, and originals with original signatures are required. For RCFEs the filing goes to the CDSS Centralized Applications Bureau. Note that the B7 program description may be a pamphlet or brochure, but only if it contains every listed element. Items marked ** in B7 may instead appear in B9 Admission Policies. Excluded as non-policy paperwork: B1 (partnership/corporate/LLC documents), B2 (administrator certification and experience verification), B3 (social worker verification, not applicable to RCFE), B12 (private-water bacteriological analysis), B16 (first aid cards), B17 (orientation certificate), B18 (group home/FFA program statement, not applicable), and all Section A forms except A14 (A1-A13, A15-A17: application, financial forms, LIC 500/501/503/508, sketch, fire inspection, etc.). B6.2 refers to RCFE regulation 87565 for the required training topics, and that section was not retrieved here. B2 states that experience verification is not necessary for a 1-6 bed RCFE. Version caution: CDSS now lists LIC 281 (11/25), but I could not retrieve its PDF. Download it from the CDSS forms page, compare it item by item against the 9/04 list above, and use any changes. The regulation-based 'plan of operation' requirement (22 CCR 87208) was not retrieved and is not included.
